title: Your TV Remote Flashes a Light You Can't See, but Your Phone Camera Can
fb_caption: Every time you press a button, your TV remote flashes an infrared LED, a light just past red that your eyes can't see. Each button sends its own pattern of super-fast flashes, and a small sensor on the TV reads it. Many phone cameras can pick up that light, so it shows up on screen as a purple-white flash. Point the remote at your phone's camera and press a button; if nothing shows, try the selfie camera. Did you see the flash?
engagement_comment: Did you see the flash? 1 = yes, on my main camera, 2 = only on the selfie camera, 3 = nothing showed up.
sources: Wikipedia, Remote control (940 nm LED typical; each button sends its own pattern of infrared pulses; the receiver recognizes the pattern; invisible to the eye but visible to digital and phone cameras, often as purple light): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remote_control
Adafruit, IR Sensor (remotes pulse an IR LED; receivers peak at 940 nm and 38 kHz): https://learn.adafruit.com/ir-sensor/overview

Carolina Biological, Seeing infrared with a phone camera (many phones have IR filters on the rear camera and little or none on the front camera; a light appears on the front camera screen): https://knowledge.carolina.com/?p=189

tts.director_notes: Calm, curious American male explainer, warm and clear, about 170 words per minute, short pause before the twist. Read only the script text.

beats.text: Your TV remote flashes a light every time you press a button. You just can't see it.
That little bulb up front is an infrared LED. Its light sits just past red, beyond what eyes can see.
Each button sends its own pattern of super-fast flashes, like Morse code made of light.
A small sensor on the TV catches that pattern and does what you asked.
Here's the trick. Many phone cameras can see that light, so it shows up as a purple-white flash.
Try it tonight. Point the remote at your phone's camera and press a button. Nothing? Try the selfie camera.
Did you see the flash? Tell us below.
